verses.text: Now when these things were done, the princes came near to me, saying, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, following their abominations, even those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy offspring  have mixed themselves with the peoples of the lands. Yes, the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this trespass.”
When I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded.
Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel were assembled to me, because of their trespass of the captivity; and I sat confounded until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I arose up from my humiliation, even with my garment and my robe torn; and I fell on my knees, and spread out my hands to Yahweh my God;
and I said, “My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to you, my God; for our iniquities have increased over our head, and our guiltiness has grown up to the heavens.

Since the days of our fathers we have been exceeding guilty to this day; and for our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests, have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.

Now for a little moment grace has been shown from Yahweh our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and revived us a little in our bondage.

For we are bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to revive us, to set up the house of our God, and to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
“Now, our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,

which you have commanded by your servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land, to which you go to possess it, is an unclean land through the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, through their abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with their filthiness.

Now therefore don’t give your daughters to their sons. Don’t take their daughters to your sons, nor seek their peace or their prosperity forever; that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children forever.’
“After all that has come on us for our evil deeds, and for our great guilt, since you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such a remnant,

shall we again break your commandments, and join in affinity with the peoples that do these abominations? Wouldn’t you be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant, nor any to escape?

Yahweh, the God of Israel, you are righteous; for we are left a remnant that has escaped, as it is today. Behold,  we are before you in our guiltiness; for no one can stand before you because of this.”

footnotes.content: The leaders bring hard news: our own people have taken on the ways of those around them, mixing themselves where they shouldn't. How does it happen? So slowly you don't see it coming—a daughter here, a son-in-law there—until the line gets fuzzy and you're walking where you meant never to walk.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The princes themselves led the way in this. That's the sting—not that the weak stumbled, but that the strong ones chose to. When leaders treat covenant lightly, the whole people slides. We've all felt that weight: what gets modeled at the top is what takes root everywhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezra tears his clothes and pulls his hair—old signs of deepest shame. His own people, the ones he'd walked with back from exile, had wandered from the path. Grief like that doesn't announce itself politely. Sometimes your body knows the weight before your words do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The remnant who trembled at God's word gathered to him, confounded together. In that silence before the evening offering—sitting in the dust of what they'd let slip away—there's something true: real believers do grieve when the Lord is dishonored, even when it costs them friendship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From his sitting shame, Ezra rises to kneel and spread his hands. Note the movement: not fleeing into denial, but rising from humiliation to face the Lord with open hands. Honest prayer begins where we are—torn garments and all—and moves toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He can't even look up. The weight of covenant-breaking—their own, and their fathers' before them—has piled so high that his shame is real and simple. No excuses, no blame-shifting. That's the beginning of repair: one person saying, 'I am ashamed,' and meaning it before the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezra traces a long line of guilt—from fathers to kings to priests to now. He doesn't separate himself from the chain. That's humility without the false distance: we inherit more than land; we inherit the fruit of broken faith too. Yet even here, there's a quiet mercy he'll come to see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After the catalog of failure comes a turn: 'Now for a little moment grace has been shown.' A nail in His holy place, a light for their eyes, a breath in their bondage. That word 'now'—it marks the hinge where Ezra sees that even exile has been held by kindness. The Lord never quit them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Still bondservants, yet the Lord extended loving-kindness in the sight of Persian kings. The wall in Judah and the house standing again—real evidences of what grace can do in broken places. God hasn't hidden His face; He's shown it in concrete mercies they can touch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now Ezra moves from confession to the unbearable question: 'What shall we say after this?' How do you answer grace? The only honest thing is to acknowledge you've forsaken what was commanded—not to hide behind pity or circumstance, but to see the full shape of your turning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets had warned plainly: the land was unclean by the peoples' abominations, and mixing with them would draw that uncleanness into Israel's own life. The word was clear; the temptation to ignore it equally clear. We often know the wise path before we choose the crooked one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command is simple: don't intermarry, don't seek friendship with those in covenant-rebellion. The promise is simple too: 'that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance forever.' Separation from idolatry isn't punishment; it's the shape of strength and permanence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here's the startling pivot: 'You have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such a remnant.' In captivity's harshness, Ezra sees mercy. Not mercy that overlooks; mercy that remains patient, that stops short of the full wage of sin. The Lord could have erased them. He didn't.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The logic is urgent: if we break His commands again after He's shown such restraint, can we expect anything but His full wrath? There's a kind of covenant maturity here—Ezra understands you can't keep taking mercy for granted. Forgiveness is real, but so is the consequence of throwing it away again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: we too stand before God in guiltiness, unable to stand on our own merit, yet held by His righteousness alone. Ezra's confession—'we are left a remnant that has escaped'—speaks to every generation that has wandered and been called home again. The only stable ground is His justice and His mercy meeting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
